clue.text: The fellow making a claim?

parts.note: a university fellow or chair holder is literally one who professes, that is, someone who declares or claims something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' suggests just a man, but here it is the academic sense, and the question mark points to the literal reading: one who professes, or declares.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior university teacher is named from the verb profess, to declare openly, so the title literally means a claimant.

clue.text: A quarter drop first-class weapon

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters or compass points
to sag is to droop or drop
A1 (written AI) means first-class or excellent

explanation.surface: Someone tries to describe an odd weapon in terms of a quarter, a drop and quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces simply sit side by side; AI stands for A1, the old Lloyd's Register mark for a first-class ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An assagai is a slender throwing spear used in southern Africa, so it is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Underwear packed for the head

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
something packed is put away in case, enclosed in a box

explanation.surface: Someone packs their underwear before heading off on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranium, the bony box enclosing the brain, forms the upper part of the skull in the head.

clue.text: Order retreat

parts.note: a religious order of monks withdraws to a secluded house; read as a command, the clue seems to say 'go back'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a military command to fall back, but 'Order' is a religious order and 'retreat' a place of seclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Communities of monks live secluded in such a house, so it is the retreat of a religious order.

clue.text: A very little pool on the street

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond, a body of standing water
ST is the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A tiny puddle has formed out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of mere, as in 'the slightest hint', means the smallest possible amount.

clue.text: Pop up to extol value

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Pa and Pop are both familiar words for a father
to extol is to praise highly

explanation.surface: A pop star's fans rise to celebrate and rate the song highly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like music or a burst, but it is a word for father; in a down entry 'up' means read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess the worth of something, as a valuer does, is to put a price on it.

clue.text: Push a number into a sailing man's transport

indicators.note: the push and the number are put into the sailor, which is enclosing them

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, a slang name for a seaman
to ram is to push or force hard
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone shoves a figure into a seaman's vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Push' looks like the verb of the surface, but it supplies a synonym; both pieces go together inside the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails in the street, a form of public transport.

clue.text: One read out for school assembly

definitions.note: a single named school; the answer is its proper name

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil is chosen to read aloud at the morning gathering in the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the seven letters of ONE READ. ROEDEAN is a well-known girls' boarding school near Brighton in England; 'for school assembly' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a famous English independent girls' boarding school on the Sussex coast.

clue.text: Husband about to start playing tennis

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
every tennis point begins with a serve, so to serve is to start play

explanation.surface: A married man is ready to begin a game of tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a noun, a married man, but it is the verb meaning to save or keep carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to use them sparingly and keep them back, a synonym of keeping in store.

clue.text: Translation of letters re papal robes

indicators.note: translating the letters moves them into a new order, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone translates a letter about the Pope's vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing or garments, especially formal dress, which includes robes.

clue.text: Slight scrap in the queue

indicators.note: the scrap is placed in the queue, which surrounds it

parts.note: a file is a line of people one behind another, a queue
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A minor squabble breaks out among people waiting in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight, and 'Slight' like a snub; really scrap is a piece of cloth, and slight means frail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slight in build is delicate and easily broken, flimsy.

clue.text: Decides not to compete due to minor injuries

definitions.meaning: a horse or player withdrawn from an event is said to be scratched from it
small surface wounds made by claws or thorns

explanation.walkthrough: 'due to' joins the two senses, so it reads as one player pulling out because of small injuries.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw an entrant is to strike them from the list; small skin abrasions made by nails or claws share the word.

clue.text: Woman in yacht that's incorrectly rigged

indicators.note: a rig set up wrongly has its parts put in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman on a boat whose sails have been badly set up.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes IN as well as YACHT; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, originally an epithet of the moon goddess Artemis.

clue.text: Mark an urban area's need of resources

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a city is a large urban area

explanation.surface: A town planner notes where the city is short of funding.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage or lack of supplies, the state of having too little.

clue.text: Spoke after a good man got suspended

indicators.note: the spoke comes after the good man in the answer

parts.note: ST, saint, a holy or good person
a rung is a crossbar or spoke, as of a ladder or chair; also, rang is the past of ring, rung the participle

explanation.surface: A virtuous man spoke up and was then hanged or suspended from office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like the past of speak but is the noun, a bar or rung.
explanation.definitionFit: Hung up, dangling from a cord or line, as beads on a thread.

clue.text: They might well offer climbers their support

definitions.text: They might well offer climbers their support

parts.words: They might well offer climbers their support
parts.note: climbers are plants such as roses that need a garden frame to grow up, not mountaineers

explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' suggests mountaineers and ropes, but they are climbing plants on a garden framework.
explanation.definitionFit: Lattice frames of light wood fixed to walls let climbing plants grow upward.

clue.text: Given a key, created a mess but looked radiant

parts.note: G is a musical key
littered means scattered rubbish about, making a mess

explanation.surface: Someone handed a key trashed the place yet looked marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: To sparkle or shine brightly, as jewels do in the light.

clue.text: Putting a point to a club, fail to express oneself clearly

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a putter is a golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A golfer at the green struggles to say what they mean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' and 'club' set a golf scene; the point is a compass point attached in front of the putter.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak in a hasty, spluttering way, as when confused or angry.

clue.text: May be investigated — indeed it's to be expected

definitions.meaning: read as probe-able, something able to be probed
likely to happen or be true

explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' is a link; the first sense is a punning split of the word into probe plus able.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as probe plus able, it means open to inquiry; ordinarily it means likely.

clue.text: Swell painter's equipment

definitions.meaning: a long heavy wave rolling in from the sea
a cylinder used by a decorator to spread paint

explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like the old slang for splendid, but it is a sea wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A long sea wave and a decorator's cylinder for applying paint share the word.

clue.text: Concerning everybody, generally speaking

definitions.meaning: taking everything into account, on the whole

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means total or including everyone; as an adverb it means on the whole.

clue.text: Slow admitting twitch is grating

indicators.note: letting the twitch inside, so the slow word surrounds it

parts.note: late means slow or behind time
a tic is a twitch or nervous spasm

explanation.surface: A slow nervous twitch is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' looks like an adjective, irritating, but it is the noun, a grid of bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework of crossed strips forming a grid, like a grille.

clue.text: Reptiles found in Antigua -nasty creatures

indicators.note: the letters are found within the run of the clue words Antigua and nasty

explanation.surface: Unpleasant beasts lurk on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creatures' only fills out the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Large tropical lizards of the Americas, a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Getting away from it all, having taken off

definitions.meaning: airborne, as a plane after take-off

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are of escape: running away, and being up in the air in a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeing is being on the run; airborne is aboard a plane after take-off, as in airline meals.

clue.text: Approaching a raw beginner in dire straits

indicators.note: the pieces are put in the dire straits, which surround them

parts.note: being in need means being in poverty or dire straits

indicators.note: the beginner of raw is its first letter

explanation.surface: A complete novice gets close to disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raw beginner' looks like a novice, but it gives only the first letter of raw.
explanation.definitionFit: Came closer to, drew near; the clue's participle stands for the act of getting close.

clue.text: Inordinately brave without faltering — note this shows backbone

definitions.note: singular here, while the answer is plural: the bones that together form the backbone

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rearranged brave wraps round the other pieces
inordinately means excessively or wildly, signalling the letters are disordered

parts.note: er is the sound of someone faltering or hesitating in speech
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone shows great unhesitating courage, proof of real backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inordinately' rearranges brave, and 'without' wraps it round the hesitation sound and the sol-fa note. 'this shows' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine is built of these small bones stacked in a column.

clue.text: A soldier stationed by gallery when there's trouble

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A soldier is posted beside an art gallery in case of unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stationed by' just places the pieces side by side; 'trouble' is a verb, to disturb.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb or make anxious, to stir up.

clue.text: Edge between a couple of scholars to get a percussive instrument

indicators.note: the edge sits between the two scholars

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a graduate degree
BA, Bachelor of Arts, the other graduate degree
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Two academics are lined up to play in the percussion section.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wooden xylophone with resonators, played with mallets.

clue.text: Boost given by working out at eleven — no end of it

indicators.note: working out a puzzle reorders its parts, so these letters are rearranged
the last letter of eleven is dropped

explanation.surface: A gym-goer feels lifted after a workout at eleven, which seems endless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of it' cuts eleven to ELEVE, and 'working out' rearranges AT + ELEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or lift, to give a boost upward.

clue.text: Though dispirited, boldly face the lady-killer

parts.note: blue means sad or low in spirits
to beard someone is to confront them boldly

explanation.surface: Feeling low, someone still steels themselves to confront a dangerous seducer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady-killer' looks like slang for a charmer, but it is the folk-tale figure who murdered his wives.
explanation.definitionFit: In the French folk tale he is a nobleman who murders his wives one after another.
